name: Shower Tile Replacement: Checklist for Choosing the Right Substrate and Materials

step.name: Step 1: Verify the subfloor and wall framing stability
step.text: Inspect your existing framing and subfloor for deflection, rot, or water damage before buying your finish materials. Uneven or bouncy subfloors cause rigid tile and stone assemblies to crack over time. If your joists or studs need shoring up, complete all carpentry and framing repairs first so your tile base sits entirely flat and stable.

step.name: Step 2: Install moisture-resistant backing boards
step.text: Hang approved cementitious or foam-core backer boards designed specifically for wet areas rather than standard drywall or basic green board. Fasten the panels with corrosion-resistant screws according to manufacturer spacing patterns. Seal and tape all panel seams using alkali-resistant mesh tape and modified thin-set mortar to ensure a rigid, unified surface.

step.name: Step 3: Apply an approved continuous waterproofing membrane
step.text: Coat the assembly with a liquid-applied or sheet waterproofing membrane meeting ANSI A118.10 standards across shower walls, curbs, and niches. Ensure full coverage without pinholes, extending properly over transitions and corners. Water will travel past tile and grout, so this dedicated membrane serves as your true defense against concealed framing leaks.

step.name: Step 4: Check slopes and perform leak testing on shower pans
step.text: Confirm that your shower pan or sloped floor pitches properly toward the drain to eliminate puddling. Before setting a single tile, plug the drain and conduct a continuous flood test to guarantee the basin holds water without leaking into the subfloor. Catching a seepage issue right now prevents tearing out finished stone later.

step.name: Step 5: Lay out cuts and directional movement joints
step.text: Dry-fit your tile layout to balance cuts evenly across walls and prevent tiny slivers in visible corners. Plan movement joints at room perimeters and inside vertical corners rather than packing those seams with rigid grout. Use the TCNA-recommended trowel notch size for your specific tile dimensions to achieve complete mortar coverage underneath.

step.name: Step 6: Set tile and apply flexible sealant at plane changes
step.text: Spread compatible mortar using directional troweling and firmly press tiles in place to collapse ridges and eliminate hollow voids. After the mortar cures completely, pack your grout joints cleanly and immediately wash away excess haze. Finish by filling all inside corners, floor-to-wall transitions, and fixture junctions with flexible sealant instead of grout.
